value.name: Dominant GDAP1 patient fibroblast redox and respiration study
value.description: Six patient lines came from two unrelated families: three C240Y and three R120W. Available lines and controls varied by assay. Complex-I-substrate respiration and ATP synthesis were lower in both groups, but direct complex I enzyme and oxidative-stress abnormalities were clearest in C240Y. Complex I assembly and NDUFB8 abundance were preserved; SIRT1/NRF1 abundance decreased without a mediation experiment. Resveratrol treatment for 48 hours improved pooled complex I activity at 25 micromolar; 10 micromolar had no significant effect and 50 micromolar was antiproliferative. assertion.name: H69 cholangiocyte autoantigen perturbation
assertion.cell_source: Human H69 cholangiocytes with gene knockdown, inhibitors, recombinant proteins or donor immunoglobulin
assertion.description: Parallel galectin-3 and prohibitin perturbations measured intracellular pH, bile-acid permeation and apoptosis. Results were discordant across interventions and did not establish a consistent protective autoantigen mechanism. The final IgG comparison used one IgG4-related cholangitis donor and one healthy donor and did not increase bile-acid uptake. This is a biliary epithelial experiment, not a pancreatic model or a germline variant assay.

assertion.name: Human NET, pDC and B-cell coculture
assertion.cell_source: Patient or control blood pDCs and neutrophils combined with healthy-control B cells
assertion.description: Defined cultures compare patient and control cell sources and use induced NET-containing preparations. Patient pDCs promote IFN-alpha and IgG4 output; DNase and IFNAR blockade reduce output. The human study enrolled 20 patients, but tissue, serum and culture subsets differ. Tissue controls included tumor-free cancer-resection sections. The experiments do not prove that MSU or patient anti-lactoferrin IgG4 initiates disease, and no BAFF-neutralization experiment isolates that mediator.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Patient-pDC cultures show enhanced IFN-alpha output.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The B cells are healthy-control cells; extracellular DNA and receptor-blockade effects do not identify a universal human initiating antigen.

selected_evidence.snippet: More importantly, patient pDCs cultured in the presence of NETs produced greatly increased levels of IFN-α and induced control B cells to produce IgG4 (but not IgG1) as compared with control pDCs.

assertion.name: SLC10A7-CDG patient dermal fibroblasts
assertion.description: Primary dermal fibroblasts from affected individuals are the workhorse human system for this disease and carry the two measurements that connect the calcium lesion to the glycosylation lesion in the same human cells: increased calcium influx on extracellular calcium challenge, and a selectively reduced heparan sulfate fraction. The same cells show intracellular mislocalization of glycoproteins and defective post-Golgi transport.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Calcium influx after an extracellular calcium challenge is significantly increased relative to control fibroblasts.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Fibroblasts are not an affected tissue in this disease; they report the cell-autonomous biochemical lesion but cannot show how it plays out in chondrocytes, osteoblasts or ameloblasts.

readouts.name: Calcium influx after extracellular CaCl2 challenge
readouts.interpretation: Functional confirmation in human patient cells that loss of SLC10A7 de-represses calcium entry.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Golgi Glycosylation and Glycosaminoglycan Biosynthesis Defect
modeled_mechanisms.description: The heparan sulfate proportion of total glycosaminoglycan is reduced about two-fold, with total glycosaminoglycan preserved.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Fibroblast glycosaminoglycan composition is not cartilage glycosaminoglycan composition; the cartilage measurement in the same study comes from the mouse, not from affected individuals.

readouts.name: Heparan sulfate proportion of total glycosaminoglycan
readouts.target: Golgi Glycosylation and Glycosaminoglycan Biosynthesis Defect
readouts.interpretation: Selective loss of the heparan sulfate chain class rather than a global glycosaminoglycan deficit.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Defective Post-Golgi Glycoprotein Delivery to the Extracellular Matrix
modeled_mechanisms.description: Glycoproteins are mislocalized intracellularly and post-Golgi transport to the cell membrane is defective.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: The assay reports delivery to the fibroblast plasma membrane, which is a proxy for, not a measurement of, delivery into skeletal or enamel matrix.

selected_evidence.snippet: we identify decreased heparan sulfate levels in Slc10a7-/- mouse cartilage and patient fibroblasts

assertion.name: SLC10A7 knockout HAP1 cells
assertion.description: A near-haploid human cell line knocked out for SLC10A7, used to isolate the gene's function from patient genetic background. It supplied the original demonstration that SLC10A7 restrains store-operated calcium entry, and later the demonstration of O-glycosylation defects and raised ER and Golgi calcium content.

modeled_mechanisms.description: Engineered loss of SLC10A7 increases calcium influx after thapsigargin, ionomycin and ATP or carbachol; overexpression reduces it, establishing the direction of the gene's effect in both directions.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: HAP1 is a near-haploid chronic myeloid leukaemia derivative and shares no lineage with any tissue affected in this disease; the bidirectional manipulation establishes gene function, not disease pathogenesis.

readouts.name: Store-operated calcium entry
readouts.interpretation: Loss of the negative regulator increases calcium influx; the reciprocal overexpression experiment decreases it.

modeled_mechanisms.target: Golgi Glycosylation and Glycosaminoglycan Biosynthesis Defect
modeled_mechanisms.description: Knockout cells show major O-glycosylation defects together with increased ER and Golgi calcium content, reproducing in an engineered line what patient fibroblasts show.
modeled_mechanisms.limitations: Same lineage caveat; and the manganese-supplementation rescue reported in the same study is a mechanistic probe of COSMC metal sensitivity, not a therapeutic finding.

selected_evidence.snippet: SLC10A7 knockout HAP1 cells showed significantly increased calcium influx after thapsigargin, ionomycin and ATP/carbachol treatment

value.description: Nonisogenic patient fibroblasts and age/sex/passage-matched controls were compared for elastin deposition, splicing and signaling. Reduced insoluble elastin and abnormal deposition accompanied allele-dependent intracellular effects. CL 1 lacked the measured stress response; CL 4 mainly increased BiP; CL 3 showed BiP, phospho-eIF2alpha and cleaved-caspase3 changes. Increased pSMAD2 was observed across all three tested patient cultures.
value.notes: Not all six clinical participants supplied the mechanistic cultures. Biopsy sites differ, there is no allele correction or selective stress/TGF-beta rescue, and measured insoluble elastin does not establish crosslink density per molecule. Co-occurrence does not prove an obligatory retention→ER stress→apoptosis chain.

value.name: Human DHX37 depletion and catalytic-mutant complementation
value.description: HeLa RNAi and HEK293 complementation with RNAi-resistant wild-type or engineered T282A DHX37 define pre-rRNA processing and small-subunit assembly functions. Wild-type transgene rescues processing defects. Purified recombinant-protein experiments independently show RNA-dependent ATPase activity and stimulation by directly interacting UTP14A. The catalytic mutant retains the protein-presence function that prevents aberrant pre-rRNA turnover, separating that function from ATPase-dependent maturation.

assertion.description: Depletion and catalytic perturbation impair small-subunit maturation; complementation with wild-type DHX37 reverses the processing defect.
assertion.limitations: HeLa and HEK293 cells are not fetal gonadal or patient-derived cells. T282A is engineered, not an SRXY11 allele. The study does not test human sex determination, p53 necessity or MDM2 binding. The exact stage of human U3 release remains unresolved, and UTP14A-depletion effects on U3 retention may be secondary to an earlier processing block.
